Kevin Trudeau's guest, trainer and health coach Dylan Giamelli, says most people get biohacking wrong.

They picture expensive gadgets, supplements and millions of dollars spent on therapies. His real definition: taking care of yourself and depending less on other people for your own health.

His two simplest examples: walk outside in the morning, and actually fix what's on your plate. That's biohacking in its most basic form, before any gadget gets involved.

Kevin Trudeau's guest, health coach Dylan Giamelli, says most doctors run the basics and stop there - because a deeper panel can get flagged by your insurance company if it's ordered too often.

His point: you don't have to wait on a standard checkup to find out what's really going on. An independent panel can look at things a basic visit skips, like heavy metal and micronutrient levels.

His warning: labs change where the "normal" range sits, so a result that reads as fine on paper can still mean something is off underneath.

Kevin Trudeau's guest, health coach Dylan Giamelli, breaks down why your body actually ages.

His simple version: your cells have a tiny power plant inside called the mitochondria. As you get older, that power plant slows down and your cells start filling up with waste, like a trash can nobody empties.

Once that junk overflows, he says it spreads through your body - and that's where disease and inflammation take root.

The upside: your body already has a repair system for this - sleep, movement and real food are what keep it running.

What's one thing you could do today to help your cells repair?

Kevin Trudeau's guest, trainer and health coach Dylan Giamelli, lists what's actually driving testosterone down for men in the US.

First on his list: a bad diet, loaded with sugar and foods sprayed with chemicals.

Second: alcohol. His research found even one drink works against testosterone - not just heavy drinking.

Third: the basics most people skip - high stress, poor sleep, and not enough sunlight.
